title: test(scenarios): measured 30 s budget for the two skill-evals --regrade command tests
body:
<!-- claude-projects-attribution: {"github_login":"os-warren"} -->
_Requested by **Warren** · [project thread](https://claude.ai/code/project/chan_01U5RdnAAmkSQmZbqh6FtqZ8?thread=cmsg_01U5RdnAAmkSQmZbqh6FtqZ8LvPEHAQYchQkNdLqwBqea3)_

Fixes #35110

Clause-②: no
Metadata-protocol: none

## 维护者速读

- 改了什么:skill-evals 测试文件里两条跑完整 `executeRound` + `regradeRound` 的 `--regrade` 命令测试,改用具名的 30 秒超时(`REGRADE_COMMAND_TEST_TIMEOUT_MS`),不再吃 vitest 默认 5 秒;断言一条未动。
- 为什么改:merge queue 把 scenarios 和 plugin-security 排在同一个 Test Core 分片时,这条测试实测 6.2 秒、9.7 秒,超时把 #34709 两次踢出队列;本地只要 36–168 毫秒。
- 风险与回滚:只动测试文件,不发布任何东西;真挂死时最多多等 25 秒才报红。回滚即 revert 这一个 commit。
- 先看:`packages/qa/scenarios/test/skill-evals/skill-evals.test.ts` 顶部新增常量及其注释(测量来源与取值理由),以及两处 `}, REGRADE_COMMAND_TEST_TIMEOUT_MS);`。
- 两分钟验证:`pnpm --filter @objectstack/scenarios exec vitest run test/skill-evals/skill-evals.test.ts`,预期 36/36 通过。
- 需要你做的:无,席位落地。

## What changes

`packages/qa/scenarios/test/skill-evals/skill-evals.test.ts` only:

- A named constant `REGRADE_COMMAND_TEST_TIMEOUT_MS = 30_000` near the top of the file, with a comment citing the queue measurements it is sized from. This follows the package's existing convention (`STAND_IN_TEST_TIMEOUT_MS = 30_000` in `test/runner/units.test.ts`, the measured `30_000` budgets in `test/runner/external-driver.test.ts`).
- It is passed as the per-test timeout of the two tests that run a full `executeRound` and then `regradeRound`:
  - line 362 of the old file, "the command: a reworded case keeps its record bytes ..." (the test the card names);
  - "--regrade keeps a recorded trigger case planned and regrades it from its record" (the sibling on the same path).
- Every assertion is kept. No skip, no retry, no quarantine, no package-wide `testTimeout`.

## Tests

Timings, per test (ms):

| Where | reworded-case test (card) | trigger-case `--regrade` sibling | file |
|:--|--:|--:|--:|
| CI, merge-queue job 134498092500 (shard 7/10, beside plugin-security) | 6218 (timed out) | not reported | 7134 |
| CI, merge-queue job 134551614597 (same plan) | 9728 (timed out) | 141 | 10526 |
| CI, merge-queue job 134557796904 (shard 8/10, light) | 2356 | under the reporter's threshold | 3149 |
| local, unloaded, 3 runs before the change | 168 / 35 / 36 | 40 / 47 / 35 | tests 239–380 |
| local, 12 CPU burners on 4 cores | 79 | 107 | tests 564 |
| local, 24 CPU burners on 4 cores | 102 | 106 | tests 848 |
| local, after the change | 40 | 52 | 36/36 pass |

How the timeout is sized: the slowest observed reading is 9728 ms; the unloaded CI reading is 2356 ms. 30 s is about 3x the slowest observed and about 13x the unloaded CI reading, and it is the budget this package's other measured suites already use.

Where the cost sits: in the same CI job the reworded-case test took 9728 ms while the sibling on the identical `executeRound` + `regradeRound` path took 141 ms, and the `executeRound`-only tests took tens of ms. So the cost lands on the first `regradeRound` call in the file, not on the round the test builds; the one thing that call does that the later one does not is a cold first run of `runnerSha` (two `git` spawns over the checkout). CPU oversubscription locally (up to 6x) did not reproduce it, and a fresh worktree's first `git status` over the same pathspec took 141 ms here, so the mechanism is not established. Because the cost follows whichever of the two runs first (a `-t` filter or a reorder moves it to the sibling), both tests get the budget, although the sibling does not measure within 2x of 5 s locally. The product code is unchanged: the measurement does not show a product-side cost that a behaviour-preserving change in `src/skill-evals/**` would remove.

## Acceptance notes

- The CI cost of the first `regradeRound` call is located (first call against second, same job) but its mechanism is not reproduced locally. If a later reading shows the cost growing past this budget, `runnerSha` (the `git rev-parse` + `git status` pair in `src/skill-evals/cli.ts`) is the place to measure first.
- No changeset: the diff touches a test file only, which is not in the package's `files[]` (`dist`, `README.md`, `CHANGELOG.md`), so nothing publishes; `skip-changeset` rides this create.
- No ablation: the diff changes a test timeout, not a tested behaviour.
